Processing
FLAC collection redistributed through Commons, with a Wikimedia MP3 access derivative. Documented

[1] [3]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms. Inferred, not documented

Bach died in 1750. This does not clear a separately protected modern performing edition.

[2]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — explicit public-domain recording release by Musopen (Commons PD-author). Documented

The opened file-description wikitext distinguishes recording={{PD-author|Musopen}} from the separate composition-only PD-old-auto-expired tag. The upstream collection explicitly says the project purchased and released recordings to the public domain, including the Goldberg Variations; its Public Domain Mark alone is not the basis.

[1] [3]

Johann Sebastian Bach, Goldberg Variations, opening Aria; Shelley Katz, piano. Musopen public-domain recording release, distributed through Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons. Session date and place unknown; streamed without editorial audio edits. Rights statement

  1. Wikimedia Commons — Goldberg Variations, Opening Aria — File description, performer attribution, original source, sound-recording licensing and transcode information.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Bach-⁠Archiv Leipzig — Johann Sebastian Bach: a chronology — Composer’s life dates and the cited career chronology.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Internet Archive — Musopen Collection as FLAC — Description explicitly states the purchase and public-domain release of recordings and lists Goldberg Variations; completion in 2012, not a documented Katz session date.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Mutopia 979 — Goldberg Variations, Aria — JD Erickson engraving from Bach-⁠Gesellschaft, CC BY-SA 3.0; two repeated sixteen-bar halves, independent bass and ornamented upper line.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Netherlands Bach Society — BWV 988 — Publication in 1741, bass foundation of the thirty variations and caution about the Goldberg commission legend.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Goldberg Variations — publication and surviving sources — Original title-page specification, Nuremberg publisher Balthasar Schmid, Forkel’s 1802 account, and distinction between the 1725 notebook and Anna Magdalena’s later Aria entry.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
